meta.titre: Africa and the Second World War: participation, hardship and the road to nationalism
meta.sous_theme: Ways Africans took part in the war and its effects on colonial rule

sections.contenu_markdown: In August 1940 the French Cameroons declared for General de Gaulle's Free France, one of the first territories in Africa to do so. Africans were soon fighting, carrying loads, building airfields and producing materials for a war that began in Europe. At Advanced Level you are asked to name the ways in which Africans took part, and then to explain how the war changed colonial rule. This course separates the two kinds of question and shows how to argue the second.

items: The Second World War lasted from 1939 to 1945, between the Allies (Britain, France, the Soviet Union, later the USA) and the Axis (Germany, Italy and Japan).
Most of Africa was ruled by European powers, and colonial subjects had no say in the decision to enter the war.
Nationalism is the demand of a people for self-government.
Raw materials are products such as minerals and crops that are used in industry.

sections.titre: Africa in the Second World War: participation and effects
sections.contenu_markdown:
### How Africans took part
| Way | Details |
|---|---|
| Soldiers | African troops served in colonial armies such as the King's African Rifles and the Royal West African Frontier Force, and in the Free French forces. Africans fought in North Africa, in East Africa against the Italians, in Madagascar and in Burma. |
| Labourers and carriers | Many Africans worked as porters, drivers, dock workers and builders of roads and airfields. In many places labour was forced. |
| Producers | Colonies supplied rubber, tin, palm products, cocoa, groundnuts, cotton and minerals. Governments fixed prices and set quotas. |
| Bases and routes | Ports and airfields such as Takoradi on the Gold Coast, Freetown and Mombasa were used by the Allies. |
| Battlefield | North Africa and parts of East Africa were battlefields, and the French territories were divided between supporters of Free France and Vichy. |

Ethiopia, occupied by Italy since 1936, was freed in 1941 and Emperor Haile Selassie returned.

### Effects of the war
| Area | Effect |
|---|---|
| Economy | Shortages of imported goods, inflation, price control and forced crops caused hardship; trade and towns grew in some places |
| Society | Ex-servicemen had seen the wider world and the weakness of Europeans, and many had grievances over pay, pensions and jobs |
| Political ideas | The Atlantic Charter of 1941 spoke of the right of peoples to choose their government, although Churchill said it did not apply to the colonies; Allied propaganda praised freedom |
| Colonial powers | Britain and France were weakened, while the USA and the Soviet Union, critical of colonial empires, became more powerful |
| Reform and protest | The Brazzaville Conference of 1944 promised reforms in French Africa but not independence; the Pan-African Congress at Manchester in 1945 demanded freedom, with Kwame Nkrumah and Jomo Kenyatta among those present |

The war did not by itself bring independence, which came mostly after 1950. Libya became independent in 1951, Ghana in 1957 and Cameroon in 1960. The war speeded up forces already at work, such as nationalist movements and the discontent of educated Africans.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks in what ways Africans took part or contributed.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give distinct ways (fighting, labour, raw materials, bases) with one fact for each. Do not write about the causes of the war.

variantes.nom: Question on impact or on nationalism
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks about the effects of the war or whether it caused nationalism.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Group the effects (economic, social, political, international), give evidence for each, and compare the war with other causes before giving a verdict.

sections.enonce_markdown: Assess the impact of the Second World War on the growth of nationalism in Africa.

etapes.justification: 'Assess' asks for the importance of the war among other causes.
etapes.resultat_markdown: I must prove the war's impact and compare it with other causes.
African soldiers served overseas, learned that Europeans could be beaten, and returned with grievances about pay and jobs that made them ready to join nationalist movements.

etapes.action: Show the economic and political effects.
etapes.justification: These are the main long-term causes in the argument.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Shortages, inflation and forced crops caused anger. The Atlantic Charter and Allied talk of freedom raised hopes, and the weakness of Britain and France reduced their power to resist.

etapes.justification: Assessing includes saying what the war did not do.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Nationalist movements existed before the war and independence came mostly after 1950, so other causes, such as the growth of education and urban populations, also mattered.
The war was an important accelerator but not the only cause.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer (key points)**: The Second World War had a large impact on nationalism in Africa. African soldiers and workers gained new experience and grievances, economic hardship caused anger, the Atlantic Charter raised hopes of self-determination, and the weakening of Britain and France made resistance to demands for change harder. However, nationalist movements existed before 1939 and independence came mostly after 1950, so the war was an accelerator that worked with other causes.

items.erreur_markdown: "Africans did not take part in the Second World War, which was a European war."
items.pourquoi_faux: African soldiers, labourers and producers took part, and North Africa and East Africa were battlefields.
items.correction_markdown: Name at least three ways in which Africans took part, with an example for each.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Second World War gave independence to Africa in 1945."
items.pourquoi_faux: Most African states became independent after 1950.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the war encouraged nationalism and that independence came later.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Atlantic Charter granted independence to the colonies."
items.pourquoi_faux: The Charter was a statement of principles. Churchill said it did not apply to the colonies.
items.correction_markdown: Write that it raised hopes of self-determination but did not give freedom.

items.erreur_markdown: "Cameroon was a German colony during the Second World War."
items.pourquoi_faux: Germany lost Kamerun in the First World War, and by 1939 the territory was divided between France and Britain.
items.correction_markdown: Keep the effects of the two wars apart: the First World War ended German rule in Africa, while the Second World War took place under British and French rule.

items.enonce_markdown: State two ways, other than fighting, in which Africans helped the Allied war effort.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each of two ways: working as carriers or labourers; **producing raw materials such as rubber, palm products, cocoa or minerals**; building roads and airfields; providing bases and ports.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain how the Second World War affected the economies of the African colonies.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for developed points: (1) demand for raw materials and fixed prices or quotas; (2) forced crops and forced labour; (3) shortages of imported goods and inflation; (4) growth of some towns and trade. **The answer should show both the hardship and the growth.**

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss the view that the Second World War was the most important cause of the rise of African nationalism.
items.solution_markdown: Plan: For the view: the experience of soldiers, hardship, the Atlantic Charter, the weakening of Britain and France and the rise of the USA and the Soviet Union. Against: earlier nationalist movements, the growth of education and towns, and the Pan-African movement. Judgement: **the war was a major accelerator, but not the only or the first cause, so it should be seen together with the earlier and later factors.**

items_markdown: Africans took part as soldiers, carriers and labourers, producers of raw materials, and by providing bases and ports.
North Africa and East Africa were battlefields; Ethiopia was freed in 1941.
Effects: economic hardship, ex-servicemen's grievances, new ideas of freedom, and the weakening of Britain and France.
The Atlantic Charter (1941) raised hopes; the Brazzaville Conference (1944) promised reform but not independence; the Manchester Pan-African Congress met in 1945.
The war accelerated nationalism but did not by itself cause independence, which came mostly after 1950.
Answer 'participation' and 'impact' questions differently: list ways with facts, or weigh causes.
